audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagreed with the packet and with its own whys in four rows: it gave Gangplank Level 1 at 7/10 and gave Jax Level 3, Levels 4-5 and First item.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Skill / Skill / Skill / Gangplank / Gangplank / Gangplank / Jax. The prose says exactly that — whys[0] 'neither truly owns it', whys[1] 'even stage', whys[2] 'still a wash', whys[3] 'you out-poke him', whys[5] 'bursts him through Counter Strike', whys[6] 'Jax out-scales you'. A 53.48% Gangplank win rate with the 2+ item row conceded to Jax also fits: you win by closing before his items land.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Gangplank 7/10 -> Skill 5/10, Level 3 Jax 4/10 -> Skill 5/10, Levels 4-5 and First item Jax 4/10 -> Gangplank 6/10, in both layers as one atomic group. Level 6 and 2+ items already matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The lane is timed entirely off Counter Strike but its cooldown is never given, and Leap Strike's is never given either.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 — a 17-second window at rank 1 that shrinks to 9s maxed. That shrinking is the reason your early-to-mid dominance has a shelf life, and it is the number the whole 'bait the E' plan depends on.
audit.corrected: 17s at rank 1 written into early; the 17s-to-9s shrink written into mid; Leap Strike's 8s written into early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' in two places. Riot's name is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Empower's auto-attack reset was also never mentioned.
audit.why: Empower is a 7/6/5/4/3 cooldown that turns his next attack into a burst — at rank 5 it is up every 3 seconds, so the visible wind-up rather than any cast animation is the only tell you get. The central interaction the page gets RIGHT and should keep: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not the Powder Keg's area explosion.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster-at-Arms used in whys[6] and late; Empower's auto reset and its wind-up tell added to early.

audit.why: The packet's suspect name 'Hold Counter Strike' is a false positive — Counter Strike with a leading verb.
audit.corrected: No change made on that basis.

edits.before: Jax out-scales you: Trinity Force, the E-stun reset, and Grandmaster's Might resists win a straight 1v1, so zone with kegs and never duel him.
edits.after: Jax out-scales you: Trinity Force, the Counter Strike stun, and Grandmaster-at-Arms resists win a straight 1v1, so zone with kegs and never duel him.

edits.before: Jax's early game is about denying your kegs and punishing the gap. He can walk onto a freshly placed Powder Keg and auto it down before it arms, and his Q-leap closes on you whenever your barrel is dead and your E is on cooldown. Don't place a keg he can free-hit, and never throw a Parrrley into his auto range while Counter Strike is up — he dodges the shot and every auto around it, then reactivates for the stun. Last-hit with Parrrley at max range, eat a little poke, and respect that levels 1-3 you have almost no all-in and his leap is always looming.
edits.after: Jax's early game is about denying your kegs and punishing the gap. He can walk onto a freshly placed Powder Keg and auto it down before it arms, and Leap Strike (Q) closes on you every 8s whenever your barrel is dead. Don't place a keg he can free-hit, and never throw a Parrrley into his auto range while Counter Strike is up — 17s at rank 1 — because he dodges the shot and every auto around it, then reactivates for the stun. Empower (W) is an auto reset, so the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to step back.

edits.before: This is where you stabilize and flip it. With a second keg charge you can build a chain and detonate it with Parrrley from range — and that matters because Counter Strike only dodges the basic attacks he's standing in, not the AoE keg explosion. Bait the E: poke until he burns Counter Strike, then unload your chain the moment it expires. If he commits Q-W-E anyway, hold W (Remove Scurvy) for the reactivation stun — cleanse it, heal off your missing health, and his engage becomes your free reset. Keep two charges banked so a kill is never more than one Parrrley away.
edits.after: This is where you stabilize and flip it. With a second keg charge you can build a chain and detonate it with Parrrley from range — and that matters because Counter Strike only dodges the basic attacks he's standing in, not the AoE keg explosion. Bait the E: poke until he burns Counter Strike, then unload the chain the moment it expires — that gap is 17s at rank 1 and still 9s maxed. If he commits anyway, hold Remove Scurvy for the reactivation stun — cleanse it, heal off your missing health, and his engage becomes your free reset. Keep two charges banked so a kill is never more than one Parrrley away.

edits.before: Be honest: Jax reclaims this once items come online. Trinity Force plus his Counter Strike stun and Grandmaster's Might resistances mean he can eat a single keg and still win a clean 1v1, so never fight him without a full barrel chain set up. Your edge is range and zoning — detonate kegs to keep him off you, and use global Cannon Barrage (R) to swing skirmishes elsewhere or cover a splitpush rather than dueling the duelist. Force your fights before he hits two items, then make the game about your reach, not his trade.

Your edge is range and zoning — detonate kegs to keep him off you, and use global Cannon Barrage (R) to swing skirmishes elsewhere or cover a splitpush rather than dueling the duelist. notes: The best interaction on this page is already correct and I left it alone: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks but not the Powder Keg's area explosion, which is genuinely why Gangplank beats Jax before items. The chart was the problem — four rows contradicted both the packet and the prose, including handing Jax levels 4-5 and first item, the exact two stages the whys call Gangplank's. Also fixed: Jax's ultimate was called 'Grandmaster's Might' twice; it is Grandmaster-at-Arms.
